name: rating
description: A read-only five-star score drawn by a single element: a repeated star mask over a gradient filled to value/5, so half stars and exact averages need no extra markup. Sizes with the surrounding text, fills from the line's start edge in either direction, and stays legible in forced colours.

value.description: The score, in half steps from 0 to 5. For a fraction that is not a half step, omit this and set --rating-value instead.

--rating-value.description: The score as a bare number, 0–5, for exact averages such as 4.3 (custom property). data-value wins when both are present.

--rating-color.description: Colour of the filled share (custom property). Pass a colour token.

--rating-track.description: Colour of the unfilled share (custom property).

required_attrs: aria-label stating the score in words, e.g. "Rated 4.5 out of 5"
a11y.notes: The stars are a picture of a number, so the element is an image whose name is the number. The label must state the real score — when --rating-value carries 4.3, the label says 4.3. This is a display primitive: for a rating the user sets, use radio inputs.

notes: Always change data-value and aria-label together: one is what sighted readers see, the other is what everyone else hears.
Put a review count beside it as ordinary text; the rating itself has no children.
Inside a quote it goes directly in the figure, above the text.
